facts.text: Photographer Winslow Cobblepott is played by Joe Estevez, the younger brother of Martin Sheen and uncle of Emilio Estevez and Charlie Sheen.
Director Donald G. Jackson once took sick leave from his factory job to make his first film, The Demon Lover. His employer found out and fired him.
Jackson's first film, The Demon Lover, was partly funded by a roughly $8,000 insurance payout after co-director Jerry Younkins lost fingers in a factory accident.
Madame Zora is played by Erin O'Bryan, who later ran for the U.S. House in Hawaii's 1st District as a Libertarian and got 6,243 votes (3.1%).
Winslow Cobblepott's surname is the Penguin's. In Batman Returns (1992), Danny DeVito played Oswald Chesterfield Cobblepot, a villain created in Detective Comics #58 in 1941.
Jackson's best-known film is the cult hit Hell Comes to Frogtown (1987). A frog mask from it was later reused as a costume in his Rollergator.
Madame Zora's $3.99-a-minute line echoes the 1990s Psychic Friends Network, Dionne Warwick's infomercial hotline, which reportedly earned over $100 million in profit in its first few years.
The Security Guard is played by James D. Whitworth, who appeared in other 1995 low-budget titles such as Dragon Fury and Raw Energy.
Elliot the maintenance man is played by Conrad Brooks, who was a regular in Ed Wood's 1950s films, including Plan 9 from Outer Space.
Joe Estevez (Winslow Cobblepott) doubled for his brother Martin Sheen in long shots and voice-over on Apocalypse Now (1979) while Sheen recovered from a heart attack.
Vinnie is played by Mark Williams, who also wrote the screenplay for Jackson's Rollergator and Pocket Ninjas.
The thugs' Catwoman gag is one of the film's pop-culture references. IMDb lists Batman Returns (1992) among them, along with The Exorcist and Ghostbusters.
The thugs' Saturday Night Fever shout-out: that 1977 disco hit cost only $3.5 million and grossed $237 million worldwide. The Bee Gees soundtrack sold over 40 million copies.
The film's Catwoman reference is to Michelle Pfeiffer, who got $3 million for Batman Returns (1992) and trained for months in kickboxing and whip work to do many of her own stunts.
Elliot's story of Flying Saucers over Hollywood describes Plan 9 from Outer Space. Actor Conrad Brooks was in that film, as a police officer, and played a bartender in Ed Wood.
Plan 9 from Outer Space, the film Elliot describes, had a listed budget of only $60,000. Harry and Michael Medved's 1980 book The Golden Turkey Awards crowned it the worst film ever made.
Ed Wood's Plan 9 premiered in 1957 as Grave Robbers from Outer Space. It was retitled, partly because its Baptist financiers reportedly found the original title blasphemous.
Director Donald G. Jackson was fired from Pocket Ninjas (originally Skate Dragons) by executive producer David Huey. A financing company then wanted kids' films, and the result was Baby Ghost.
Jackson's sister film Rollergator was shot guerrilla-style in fall 1995 on a Hi8 camera with no permits. Scott Shaw says Jackson later destroyed the only print in a rage.
Madame Zora admits she's a phony. In real life the Psychic Friends Network went bankrupt in 1998, reporting about $26 million in liabilities against roughly $1.2 million in assets.
Baby Ghost was riffed by Mike, Kevin and Bill of RiffTrax. Joe Estevez has starred in three RiffTrax titles, and Rollergator was called the worst movie they'd ever covered.
The Exorcist and Ghostbusters get name-checked here. IMDb lists both among the films Baby Ghost references.
Ghostbusters (1984), name-checked in Baby Ghost, earned about $229 million in its first run. Director Ivan Reitman later admitted its reported $25-30 million budget figure was made up.
Dan Aykroyd first conceived Ghostbusters as a time-and-space-hopping vehicle for himself and John Belushi. Director Ivan Reitman said it would have cost around $200 million.
Director Donald G. Jackson and Scott Shaw developed 'zen filmmaking', which uses no scripts. Jackson often used screenplays anyway to show investors, cast and crew a framework.
Tim Burton's Ed Wood (1994) won Oscars for Martin Landau as Bela Lugosi and for makeup. It cost $18 million and grossed only about $13.8 million worldwide.
Jackson's later film Ride with the Devil (1999) references Baby Ghost. Jackson died of leukemia in 2003.
Jackson's Hell Comes to Frogtown (1988) inspired the Family Guy episode Hell Comes to Quahog. Its budget grew from a planned $150,000 to somewhere between $750,000 and $1 million.
Conrad Brooks was born Conrad Biedrzycki to Polish immigrant parents. He died in December 2017 after a long run as an Ed Wood alum.
RiffTrax released its Baby Ghost riff on August 6, 2021, as part of a 'Summer of Joe Estevez' theme. It runs 86 minutes, matching the film itself.
